stem: A 4-year-old boy has delayed motor development, calf hypertrophy, a waddling gait, and a Gowers sign. Which of the following is NOT a complication of this condition?
explanation: The clinical picture is most consistent with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. It can be complicated by cardiomyopathy, contractures, and respiratory problems including sleep-disordered breathing. Optic glioma is not a complication of Duchenne muscular dystrophy; it is classically associated with neurofibromatosis type 1.
rationale: The stem describes Duchenne muscular dystrophy, making the task to identify the option that is not a known complication.

optionExplanations.A: Dilated cardiomyopathy is a well-recognised complication of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
optionExplanations.B: Limb contractures commonly develop due to progressive muscle weakness and immobility.
optionExplanations.C: Obstructive sleep apnoea can occur from nocturnal respiratory muscle weakness and sleep-disordered breathing.
optionExplanations.D: Optic glioma is not associated with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

Instructions

Question 3 - 5 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 4 year old boy visits presents to you for his planned health check and immunisations. You have never met him before. You enquire about his developmental history and learn that he walked at 2 years and is still not very stable on his feet. He also didn’t start talking until he was 22 months which his mum says ‘runs in the family’. His mother is not concerned about his hearing or vision. He has an elder sister who is 6 and is thriving in school.

On examination the boy is not dysmorphic. His weight is 15kg (25th centile) and his height is 97cm (25th centile). His head circumference is 48cm (25th centile). When you examine his gait you notice he has very large calves and he walks with a waddling gait. When you get him to rise up from lying on the floor, he turns himself over and then uses his hands to push himself up from the floor. His tone is normal; his power is 4/5 proximally at the hips and shoulders but normal peripherally. You elicit deep tendon reflexes with reinforcement. His cranial nerve exam is normal. His coordination is normal as is his sensory exam. His cardiovascular examination is normal.
